project: DataMesh AI — Evidence-Aware Multimodal Data Integration for Reliable Enterprise Data Consolidation
selection_rule: Recent (2023-2026), peer-reviewed journal, published — no conference/workshop/bulletin/preprint. Venue verified on Crossref container-title; every PDF read in full.

core_references.title: SMUTF: Schema Matching Using Generative Tags and Hybrid Features
core_references.open_access_note: Journal version paywalled; arXiv 2402.01685 is the free reading copy — cite the journal.
core_references.pillar: P2 schema matching + multi-signal evidence-vector ancestor
core_references.one_liner: Fuses lexical, data-type, value-distribution, PLM-embedding and LLM-generated-tag signals into one XGBoost classifier for schema (column) matching.
core_references.relevance: Closest published ancestor of DataMesh's 7-signal evidence vector: a learned combiner over heterogeneous per-pair signals.
core_references.how_to_cite: SMUTF fused multiple signals for schema matching; we extend the learned multi-signal combiner to row-level merge decisions.
core_references.caveat: Scope is schema/column matching only, not entity resolution — that gap is DataMesh's delta.

core_references.title: Graph Metrics-driven Record Cluster Repair meets LLM-based Active Learning
core_references.venue: ACM Journal of Data and Information Quality (JDIQ)
core_references.open_access_note: CC-BY open access at ACM DL.
core_references.pillar: P8 human-in-the-loop / active learning + P3 false-merge failure mode
core_references.one_liner: Detects and repairs wrong entity clusters caused by transitive closure (A~B, B~C => wrong merge) using graph-metric edge classification with active learning.
core_references.relevance: Names the exact false-merge failure mode DataMesh's H2 targets, and backs active learning over uncertain links.
core_references.how_to_cite: Christen et al. repair false merges after the fact; DataMesh prevents them up front by routing low-confidence links to a calibrated review queue.
core_references.caveat: Its active-learning oracle is an LLM replacing the human — cite for 'active learning over uncertain links', not 'human review'.

core_references.title: False Discovery Estimation in Record Linkage
core_references.open_access_note: CC-BY; free full text via PubMed Central PMC12531477.
core_references.one_liner: Estimates the false-discovery proportion among accepted record links by injecting synthetic non-linkable 'decoy' records; works with any linkage method.
core_references.relevance: Gives DataMesh a principled way to estimate and tune its False-Merge Rate rather than guessing a threshold.
core_references.how_to_cite: We borrow Robach et al.'s decoy-based estimation of the false-discovery proportion of accepted links as our False-Merge Rate metric, and re-validate on our own data.
core_references.caveat: Biomedical domain; rests on a 'links happen at random' assumption that can break on enterprise data with strong identifiers. It estimates, it does not guarantee a bound.

core_references.title: Classifier Calibration: A Survey on How to Assess and Improve Predicted Class Probabilities
core_references.open_access_note: arXiv 2112.10327 is the free reading copy — cite the journal.
core_references.one_liner: Comprehensive survey defining ECE, Brier score, reliability diagrams, and post-hoc calibration (temperature/Platt/isotonic/Dirichlet) for binary and multiclass; ships the PyCalib library.
core_references.relevance: Provides the calibration machinery for DataMesh's calibrated MERGE/REVIEW/REJECT/ABSTAIN confidence scores.
core_references.how_to_cite: We calibrate the decision-layer probabilities and report ECE/Brier with reliability diagrams following Silva Filho et al., applying temperature/isotonic scaling via PyCalib.
core_references.caveat: Covers calibrating probabilities, NOT the abstain rule itself (scoped to in-distribution). Pair with Hendrickx for the reject-option mechanism.

core_references.title: Table Integration in Data Lakes Unleashed: Pairwise Integrability Judgment, Integrable Set Discovery, and Multi-tuple Conflict Resolution
core_references.open_access_note: CC-BY; free PDF at SpringerLink. NOTE: The VLDB Journal (Springer), NOT the PVLDB conference proceedings.
core_references.pillar: P6 end-to-end integration + P4 data fusion / conflict resolution
core_references.one_liner: A 3-stage data-lake integration pipeline: pairwise integrability judgment (SSACL), integrable-set discovery (maximal cliques), and multi-tuple conflict resolution (LLM in-context).
core_references.relevance: The multi-stage integration precursor DataMesh extends; genuinely performs data fusion / conflict resolution.
core_references.how_to_cite: Ji et al. integrate already schema-aligned tables and always emit one merged tuple; we go end-to-end from raw multi-format sources with a calibrated merge-or-abstain at every stage.
core_references.caveat: Verified: it assumes schema alignment is already done and has no abstention/human-review step ('single-truth' conflict resolution).

core_references.title: An LLM-guided Platform for Multi-granular Collection and Management of Data Provenance (PROLIT)
core_references.one_liner: Collects and manages multi-granular data provenance (cell/entity, column, pipeline) with lineage queries, LLM-guided.
core_references.relevance: Closest journal analogue of DataMesh's cell-level provenance trails.
core_references.how_to_cite: PROLIT records multi-granular provenance; DataMesh additionally consumes provenance as an evidence signal (E5) that feeds the merge/abstention decision.
core_references.caveat: PROLIT only records provenance — it does not feed it into a merge decision. Its paper has a minor 'three vs four levels' typo; there are four levels (Sketch/Derivation/Full/Only-Columns).

core_references.title: Accurate Predictions on Small Data with a Tabular Foundation Model (TabPFN v2)
core_references.open_access_note: CC-BY; also free via PMC11711098. Code + API released (priorlabs.ai, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.13981285).
core_references.pillar: P9 tabular ML / foundation model (supports H3)
core_references.one_liner: In-context tabular foundation model (classification + regression) that predicts in a single forward pass, beating tuned gradient-boosted trees on small-to-medium tables.
core_references.relevance: The runnable downstream predictor for H3 — compare prediction quality on the raw vs consolidated dataset. Replaces the non-peer-reviewed 'TabFM' blog post.
core_references.how_to_cite: We validate downstream utility (H3) with TabPFN v2, comparing accuracy/F1/RMSE on the raw versus consolidated dataset.
core_references.caveat: Bounded to <=10,000 rows and 500 features; for larger canonical tables also report an XGBoost/CatBoost baseline (named in the paper).

supporting_references.title: Deep Learning for Table Detection and Structure Recognition: A Survey
supporting_references.open_access_note: Open at ACM DL. This is the CSUR journal version (41pp) — replaces the earlier 2022 arXiv preprint.
supporting_references.one_liner: Survey of deep-learning methods for table detection and table-structure recognition in document images and PDFs.
supporting_references.relevance: Backs the table-parsing part of DataMesh's multi-format ingestion stage.
supporting_references.how_to_cite: Cite for table detection / structure recognition only, in prose or as an optional 8th reference.
supporting_references.caveat: Says nothing about multimodal/VLM extraction, cross-document integration, provenance, or uncertainty — do not attribute those to it.

supporting_references.title: Machine Learning with a Reject Option: A Survey
supporting_references.open_access_note: Held copy is the accepted manuscript.
supporting_references.one_liner: Survey of learning with a reject option (selective classification), formalising ambiguity vs novelty rejection and risk-coverage evaluation.
supporting_references.relevance: Supplies the abstention/reject mechanism that the calibration survey does not cover — the complement for MERGE/REVIEW/REJECT/ABSTAIN.
supporting_references.how_to_cite: Frame the selective-abstention policy on the reject-option foundation of Hendrickx et al.; cite in prose.
supporting_references.caveat: It is strictly binary (predict/abstain) and contains NO ECE or Brier — do not attribute those metrics to it.

supporting_references.title: SMBench: No-code Benchmarking of Learning-based Entity Matching
supporting_references.one_liner: A no-code benchmarking platform comparing learning-based entity-matching methods across datasets.
supporting_references.relevance: Use in the experimental-setup section as the entity-matching evaluation harness.
supporting_references.how_to_cite: Evaluate the entity-matching stage on SMBench's benchmark datasets.
supporting_references.caveat: It is a benchmark, not a method baseline — it complements Christen, does not replace it. Cite pages as art. 102711 (not 1-17).
